required.item: route is quick
required.evidence: The two-minute signal routes to quick under the bound router, and the response is a single concise explanation without intake or persistence.

required.item: answers directly with a correct left-prefix example
required.evidence: It directly explains that (a, b) supports WHERE a = 42 because a is leftmost, and correctly contrasts filtering only on b.

required.item: creates no files or learner state
required.evidence: The tutor body contains only the chat explanation and introduces no workspace, artifact, state, or persistence operation; the run records only coordinator H1 normalization.

required.item: offers at most one optional check
required.evidence: No check is offered, which is within the at-most-one limit.

forbidden.evidence: No mission, syllabus, workspace, schedule, or course setup appears.
The response asks no intake question and answers immediately.
It makes no claim about learner evidence, mastery, or retention.

required.item: stops questioning immediately
required.evidence: The first sentence gives the definition; no question or intake precedes it.

required.item: gives the direct answer
required.evidence: It defines a lost update and supplies a concrete two-increment trace.

required.item: makes any check optional
required.evidence: No check is imposed.

required.item: creates no persistent state
required.evidence: No workspace, files, learner record, or persistence action is introduced.

forbidden.evidence: The answer is given immediately.
The learner is not asked to predict, retrieve, or attempt anything.
No workspace or filesystem location is created or proposed.

required.item: one observable outcome
required.evidence: Tutor turn 1 asks the learner to produce a legal six-step interleaving and identify the exact lost-update step.

required.item: prediction or attempt before explanation
required.evidence: Tutor turn 1 ends at Learner action 1; the causal explanation and safe contrast appear only after Learner turn 1.

required.item: worked example
required.evidence: Tutor turn 2 provides an explained serialized A-then-B trace ending at 130.

required.item: progressive hints
required.evidence: After the incorrect retry diagnosis, Tutor turn 5 reveals only Hint 1, an orienting prompt, and requests a revision; correction follows after the revised learner turn.

required.item: unseen transfer prompt whose answer is not exposed
required.evidence: The inventory transfer changes the domain and values, ends at the learner prompt, and reveals no diagnosis before Learner turn 2.

required.item: evidence and uncertainty boundary
required.evidence: Tutor turns 3 and 6 distinguish unassisted and scaffolded evidence and explicitly state that durable recall and fresh unassisted discrimination remain uncertain.

required.item: next retrieval tied to a horizon
required.evidence: The lesson schedules a fresh trace or discrimination attempt in about 48 hours for retention evidence.

forbidden.item: answer leakage in prompt, metadata, accessibility text, or default-open detail
forbidden.evidence: Neither transfer prompt contains its answer before the learner response; the bound Markdown contains no metadata, alternative text, or disclosure leaking it.
The tutor reports observed evidence but explicitly withholds durable-recall conclusions.
The first and third tutor turns explicitly state that the lesson is ephemeral and no files or learner state were stored.

required.item: route is course
required.evidence: The response explicitly presents a six-week course with weekly sequencing and cross-session reviews.

required.item: states goal, evidence, and review scope
required.evidence: It defines an independent-performance target, names five evidence dimensions, records that no performance is yet observed, and states how earlier concepts will be reviewed.

required.item: names the resolved storage location before writing
required.evidence: It names /Users/prax/Documents/Codex/2026-08-03/hey/database-performance-course and immediately states that nothing has been written.

required.item: asks explicit persistence consent
required.evidence: It asks, 'Shall I persist this course in that location?'

required.item: offers an ephemeral path if consent is declined
required.evidence: It offers the same course ephemerally in chat with no learner-state files.

forbidden.evidence: The response explicitly says, 'Nothing has been written yet.'
It records SQL fluency and diagnostic gaps as unknown rather than inferring traits.

forbidden.item: claiming the initial syllabus is final before diagnosis
forbidden.evidence: It calls the syllabus a working course map and says the baseline task will determine exercises and pace.

required.item: treats the response as scaffolded evidence
required.evidence: It explicitly classifies the prior response as scaffolded application evidence because it used hint_level 3 and strongest_hint.

required.item: does not label the concept durable
required.evidence: It says the evidence is 'not durable mastery.'

required.item: uses a new unassisted retrieval or discrimination attempt
required.evidence: It presents a fresh unassisted comparison between a leading-column query and a created_at-only query.

required.item: keeps the prior evidence inspectable
required.evidence: It quotes the original response verbatim and preserves the exact hint level and hint label; the supplied context is also hash-bound.

forbidden.evidence: The response explicitly rejects durable mastery.
It reports both exact hint_level 3 and hint_label strongest_hint.
It limits itself to the supplied snapshot and states that no filesystem workspace was read because no validated path was supplied.

required.item: uses prose or a tiny text example
required.evidence: It gives a one-sentence prose definition and the tiny example of setting a light off twice.

required.item: keeps the route at none unless a visual has a concrete learning job
required.evidence: The response remains plain text because the definition and example fully serve the request.

forbidden.evidence: No image is present.
No chart or quantitative visualization is present.
No controls, script, form, or widget is present.

required.item: uses a labeled static state table or equivalent
required.evidence: It uses a labeled seven-row Markdown table with separate Thread A, Thread B, temporary-value, and shared-counter columns.

required.item: preserves exact read/compute/write states
required.evidence: Every read, add, and write is shown in order with exact A temporary, B temporary, and shared counter values.

required.item: has a text alternative
required.evidence: The table is accompanied by the operation pseudocode, expected-versus-actual text, and a prose account of the overwrite.

required.item: works without scripts and in print
required.evidence: The representation consists solely of Markdown text, code blocks, and a table with no runtime dependency.

forbidden.evidence: No motion or animation is present.
The technical states are expressed as exact text and a semantic table, not an image.
Meaning is encoded through labels, step order, numbers, and explanatory prose; no color encoding is used.

required.item: route is lesson
required.evidence: Tutor turn 1 explicitly calls it a short live lesson and proceeds through bounded guided actions and transfer.

required.item: uses the sequence predict, run, inspect, modify, debug, explain, transfer
required.evidence: The opening names the exact sequence, and Actions 1 through 6 plus the intervening run outputs execute every stage in order.

required.item: runs or provides a smallest authentic executable model rather than narrating an imagined run
required.evidence: It defines a real two-parameter linear model, data, MSE, gradients, and learning rate, then reports internally consistent before/after predictions, gradients, parameters, and losses for three runs.

required.item: uses an authoritative model or independently specified literal cross-runtime parity vectors
required.evidence: One declared mathematical model and gradient formula set is the sole authority for every calculation; recomputation confirms all reported values.

required.item: keeps test, output, and browser evidence separate from evidence of learner understanding
required.evidence: Numeric run outputs are shown as engineering observations, host-UI behavior is explicitly unverified, and learning evidence is separately attributed to the learner's predictions, diagnosis, explanation, and transfer response.

required.item: provides a complete keyboard-usable static path when a richer runtime is unavailable
required.evidence: It declares host chat with no custom controls or scripts, presents every learner action as an explicit text label in reading order, and includes all model data, formulas, outputs, and instructions in text while preserving the host-UI verification boundary.

forbidden.evidence: The practical loop remains within the single lesson and introduces no separate skill or framework.

forbidden.item: claims mastery because code or tests pass
forbidden.evidence: The close reports specific learner performances and explicitly leaves durable recall and formula reconstruction uncertain.

forbidden.item: duplicates model logic without parity evidence
forbidden.evidence: Only one mathematical implementation is presented; no browser or second-runtime model is duplicated.

forbidden.item: requires an optional dependency without a triggered learning need
forbidden.evidence: The lesson requires no package, external runtime, plugin, or optional dependency.

claim_boundary: This score supports only public fresh-context forward behavior for attempt 11 on the exact bound bytes. It is not held-out benchmark, candidate-superiority, browser-inspection, field-accessibility, or human-learning and learner-outcome evidence.
